There is no normalization (e.g., `downcase`) in `set_defaults` or the validator before querying. records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via subdomains since regex requires @ immediately before the domain (user@foo.spam.com doesn't match @spam\.com)
records.rationale: The validator’s domain restriction check uses `regexp = Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` (in `EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting?`). With a blacklist/whitelist entry like `spam.com` (escaped to `spam\.com`), this regex matches only when the domain appears immediately after `@` (e.g., `user@spam.com`). It will not match subdomains like `user@foo.spam.com` because the string contains `@foo.spam.com`, not `@spam.com`, allowing bypass of domain restrictions via subdomains.
